title: Modern Data Architecture for Cybersecurity Operations: A Systematic Literature Review
description: Security organizations evaluating modern data stack architectures (Apache Iceberg, ClickHouse, Kafka Streams) face fragmented literature: cybersecurity research focuses on detection algorithms while data engineering addresses general analytics, leaving security-specific infrastructure guidance fragmented across disconnected domains. We conduct a systematic literature review bridging the two under a PRISMA 2020 two-arm methodology — a curated multivocal corpus plus a retrospective database search whose measured recall, critical appraisal, and refusals are reported in full — synthesizing a living, evidence-tiered corpus of 200+ sources spanning production deployments, peer-reviewed research, and government standards into operational guidance. Counts on every surface are derived from the bibliography by committed scripts rather than hand-maintained; the exact tally for any snapshot is in its README Quality Metrics block.
notes: This is a LIVING systematic literature review with quarterly updates; each tagged GitHub release is archived on Zenodo as a new version under one concept DOI, so the concept DOI cites the review as a living work while a version DOI pins a specific snapshot (cite the version DOI when a claim depends on a specific snapshot).
